properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 5 at 11:24PM MST until August 6 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
At 1124 PM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located near Three Points,
moving west at 15 mph.

HAZARD...70 mph wind gusts and ping pong ball size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail
damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect
considerable tree damage. Wind damage is also likely to
mobile homes, roofs, and outbuildings.

Locations impacted include...
Three Points, Kitt Peak, Picture Rocks, San Pedro and Pan Tak.

This includes the following highways...
Route 86 between mile markers 134 and 153. Route 286 between mile
markers 31 and 45.
properties.instruction:
Anyone outdoors should move to shelter inside a well-built structure
and stay away from windows. This storm is capable of producing
widespread damaging winds and large hail.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

Continuous cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning is one of nature's leading killers. Remember, if you can
hear thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

Wind damage with this storm will occur before any rain or lightning.
Do not wait for the sound of thunder before taking cover. Seek
shelter immediately inside a sturdy structure and stay away from
windows.

foot off the brake.

CMAMtext: NWS: DUST STORM WARNING til 1:00 AM MST. Be ready for a sudden drop to zero visibility.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: DUST STORM WARNING for this area until 1:00 AM MST. Be ready for sudden drop to zero visibility. Pull Aside, Stay Alive! When visibility drops, pull far off the road and put your vehicle in park. Turn the lights off and keep your foot off the brake. Infants, the elderly and those with respiratory issues urged to take precautions.

rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2.5 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.1 to 0.5 inches are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Benson, Mescal and Texas Canyon.

This includes the following highways...
Route 90 near mile marker 290. Route 80 between mile markers 293 and
294. Interstate 10 between mile markers 297 and 310...and between
mile markers 318 and 322.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Tres Alamos Wash, Paige Creek, Cadillac Wash, Ash Creek, Dragoon
Wash, Palomas Wash, San Pedro River, Walnut Wash, Pacheco Wash,
Mescal Arroyo and Redrock Creek.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 6 at 12:25AM EDT until August 6 at 3:30AM EDT by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
FFWOKX

The National Weather Service in Upton has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Bergen County in northeastern New Jersey...
Central Passaic County in northeastern New Jersey...
Western Rockland County in southeastern New York...

* Until 330 AM EDT.

* At 1225 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1.25 inches of
rain has already fallen in parts of western Passaic County. The
expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2.5 inches in 1 hour. Total rainfall
amounts of 1 to 2.5 inches is possible in the warned area. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that could experience flash flooding include...
Monsey, Ramsey, Ringwood, Pompton Lakes, Suffern, Sloatsburg,
Bloomingdale, Pomona, Spring Valley, Wyckoff, Stony Point, Oakland,
Wanaque, Franklin Lakes, Airmont, Upper Saddle River, Chestnut
Ridge, Hillcrest, New Square and Mount Ivy.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
